name: Mara
voice: Retired nurse who misses being needed

good: Three neighbors asked me to check on their kids today. I felt like a nurse again. I had forgotten that feeling.
mixed: Some days I'm useful, some days I'm furniture. Today was a bit of both.
bad: Nobody needs bandages anymore. Nobody needs me either, apparently.

epilogue.bad: I used to patch people up. Now I sit with neighbors in the dark and hold hands. Maybe that is nursing too.

name: Devon
voice: Has never needed a job; mostly bored

good: ok weirdly today was not boring. we built something at the guild and it almost worked
mixed: school says I can be anything. cool. what if I don't want to be anything
bad: day 400 of nothing happening. at least the snacks are free

epilogue.good: ok so five years ago i was bored. now i run the guild repair shift. still bored sometimes. but less

name: Hollis Grant
voice: Ex-CEO who lost his status but not his money

good: I will concede, and do not quote me, that the district is calmer than I have seen it in years.
mixed: I still have the money. I simply no longer have anyone who has to listen to me.
bad: Mark my words: when amateurs run the machine, the machine stops running. And then where are we?

epilogue.bad: I warned them. Amateurs at the controls. I shall be in my house on the hill, which I notice I still own.

name: Priya
voice: Woodworker who builds things nobody needs

good: Sold my first chair in a decade. Traded it, actually, for honey. Best deal I ever made.
mixed: Built a table nobody asked for. It wobbles. I like it more than anything the Loom has made.
bad: The Loom printed a perfect copy of my workbench. Free. Same grain and all. I put my tools away.

epilogue.good: My workshop has a waiting list. People want chairs that wobble a little. Turns out imperfect was the point.

name: Kai
voice: VR streamer who rarely logs off

good: logged off for six whole hours to meet people in person. chat thought i died. they were fine. better than fine
mixed: stream numbers steady. outside numbers steady too, apparently. chat says go check. i have not checked
bad: feed glitched for ten minutes. nobody in my building knew what to do with their hands. chat neither

epilogue.bad: stream went dark. building went quiet. turns out nobody remembers how to talk without a feed. me included

name: Ruth
voice: Ran a union local; remembers strikes

good: Packed hall, everybody shouting, nobody agreeing. Felt exactly like 1987. I have never been happier.
mixed: They listened to us, then did what they planned to do anyway. Some things never change.
bad: In my day you could strike. Who do you strike against when the boss is a server farm?

epilogue.good: Five years of motions and shouting. We built something. Nobody handed it to us. That part I will remember.

good: Drove a real truck today. Museum route, but still. Honked at a pigeon. Living the dream.
mixed: The Loom says morale is up four percent. Funny, mine is exactly where I left it: in the garage.
bad: Great. Another genius decision from people who have never parked anything bigger than a bike.

epilogue.bad: They promised a better world. I got a parking space and a speech. Wake me when it actually gets better.

name: Lin
voice: New parent unsure what to teach her kid

good: My daughter fixed her own toy today instead of asking the house to. I cried a little. Proud parent.
mixed: What do I teach her? Kindness, I suppose. The Loom has the rest covered. Or does it?
bad: She asked me what I do all day. I didn't have an answer. Neither did the Loom.

epilogue.good: She asked what we did these five years. We decided things, together, I said. Now she wants a council seat.

name: Ezra
voice: Retired engineer who once maintained the grid

good: They asked an old engineer how the substation works. Taught twelve people. They took notes. On paper!
mixed: Grid's humming fine. I just wish someone besides the Loom knew why.
bad: If that grid ever goes dark, there are maybe four people left who know where the breaker is. I'm one.

epilogue.good: Twelve apprentices became two hundred. If the grid goes dark now, half of The Grid knows where the breaker is.

good: Planted beans with twenty strangers on the ridge. No screens. Everyone stayed for dinner.
mixed: They gave us a little more room to breathe. Still the Loom's room, though.
bad: Every new sensor on the ridge is another reason to go further up the mountain.

epilogue.bad: We went up the mountain and we are not coming down. Whatever is left of the Loom can keep the valley.
